page.layout: One printed page. Running head at top right above the text. Marginal reference "Cap.19." in the left margin beside the first lines. Main text in one column: running text, a centred division heading "EXERC. XL.", a subheading "DE HYDROPHOBIA.", then a paragraph beginning with a large initial H. Last line "Ipsum" at the right below the text.

main_text.p: fluere mulieribus solet. Igitur quæ proprie dicuntur, sanguis funt uitiatus, ueluti nobis oftendit philosophus libro de Historia animalium tertio. Quæ menstrua (inquit) appellamus plurima fieri in mulieribus solent: quod genus sanguinis uitiatum, ægrotansq;, fluit immodicè, atq; profluuium ob eam rem dictum est. Galenus quoq; libro, de Vsu partium, decimoquarto, menstrua uocat sanguinem superfluum, quem natura singulis menfibus per uenas ad uterum pertinentes excernit.Cap.19.
main_text.head: EXERC. XL.
DE HYDROPHOBIA.
main_text.p: HYdrophobiam morbu esse totius substantiæ Fernelianis libenter concedimus, non tamen eo sensu, quo illorum præceptor libro de Abditis rerum causis secundo capite decimo intellexit, sed quod solis profligatur medicamentis, quæ proprietate totius substantiæ nostra mutare corpora possint, tamen sub calida & sicca intemperie uenenata constituit, quemadmodum postea demonstrabimus. Hoc autem miserrimum morbi genus nomen sympto-matis, quod ipsum consequitur, delumpsit.

page.notes: The first word of the heading paragraph is a large initial "H" joined with "Ydrophobiam". The marginal reference "Cap.19." is printed in the left margin; its mark is printed as "Cap.19." without a separate letter. Line-end words "sanguis" and "substantiæ" are as read; "constituit" and "miserrimum" are uncertain readings and should be checked against the scan. The final line "Ipsum" is set apart at the right and is the catchword for the next page, so it is treated as a catchword in the bottom margin rather than as text. Words marked as uncertain: "sanguis" (may read "sanguinem"), "uitiatus" and "ægrotansq;" are read from the scan with doubt, and the text "fluit" may be a misreading of "fluit" with a broken ligature. Lines near the foot are partly obscured by print show-through and should be verified.
